newsitem.title: DUBAI: Hearing for British nurses in Saudi set for Monday.
newsitem.headline: Hearing for British nurses in Saudi set for Monday.

text.p: The lawyer of two British nurses charged with killing an Australian colleague in Saudi Arabia said on Sunday the first court hearing in the murder case would be held on Monday.

"There will be a first hearing tomorrow (Monday) at noon (0900 GMT)," Saudi lawyer Salah al-Hejailan told Reuters. "It's not expected to last more than an hour or an hour and a half, maybe two hours at most. It is a preliminary hearing."
Hejailan said it was not yet clear whether Deborah Parry, 41, and Lucille McLauchlan, 31, would appear in court.

The two women have been charged with the murder of nurse Yvonne Gilford, 55, in her dormitory room at the King Fahd medical complex in the eastern oil city of Dhahran on December 11. She had been stabbed, bludgeoned with a hammer and suffocated.

The women have been imprisoned in the nearby city of Dammam since December. If convicted of murder, they could face public beheading by the sword, the first time Western women would have been executed in the conservative Islamic kingdom.
Hejailan said the preliminary hearing would cover issues such as power of attorney and schedule future court sessions.
"They will also fix a date for the prosecutor to read his report and outline the list of evidence," he said.
"We will be getting a copy of that and then we will respond to each (piece) of evidence. We may need many hearings for that. Maybe we need examinations, maybe we need special tests," Hejailan added.
Saudi police said the nurses confessed to the murder and the confessions had been filed with Saudi judges.
But Hejailan's firm said the women had withdrawn their confessions, and one of them retracted a statement that she had had a lesbian relationship with the victim.

"Still the position of my clients is that they haven't done it," Hejailan said. "They have retracted everything. The formal position of my clients is still as it was declared before that they have retracted their confession and they have not done any act."
